grammar.label: lexical cohesion — chains, substitution and elegant variation
grammar.form: repetition, synonym, superordinate, general noun (the matter, the issue, the device)
grammar.meaning: holds a text together by what the words mean, not by grammar

explanation.en: A text coheres partly through words that keep pointing at the same thing: bridge, the crossing, the structure, it. Repetition is clearer than variation; the old advice to vary every word produces 'elegant variation', where 'the bridge', 'the span' and 'the edifice' leave the reader wondering whether three things are being discussed.
explanation.uz: Matn bir narsaga ishora qiluvchi so'zlar orqali bog'lanadi: bridge, the crossing, the structure, it. Takrorlash aniqroq; har safar so'zni almashtirish o'quvchini chalkashtiradi.

grammar.positive_example: The bridge closed in March. The crossing has not reopened.
grammar.negative_example: The bridge closed in March. The span, that noble edifice, has not reopened.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek yozuvida takrorlashdan qochish an'anasi bor; ingliz ilmiy uslubida aniqlik takrordan ustun turadi.

grammar.label: thematic progression — how each sentence starts from the last
grammar.form: constant theme; linear theme (the rheme of one sentence becomes the theme of the next); derived theme
grammar.meaning: decides whether a paragraph feels like a chain or a list

explanation.en: Each sentence's first element is its theme. If every sentence has the same theme, the paragraph describes one thing. If each sentence begins from the end of the last, the paragraph builds a chain. If all the themes derive from one idea stated at the top, it fans out. Paragraphs that feel disjointed usually have no pattern at all.
explanation.uz: Har bir gapning birinchi qismi — mavzu. Barcha gaplarda bir xil mavzu bo'lsa — tavsif; har biri oldingisining oxiridan boshlansa — zanjir. Uzuq-yuluq xatboshilarda odatda hech qanday naqsh yo'q.

grammar.positive_example: The dam changed the river. The river fed four villages. Those villages are now empty.
grammar.negative_example: The dam changed the river. Four villages are now empty. The river fed them once.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida so'z tartibi erkin bo'lgani uchun mavzu-rema tuzilmasi ko'rinmaydi; ingliz tilida u so'z tartibiga bog'langan.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: This paragraph has four good sentences and no order.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: They are all about the reservoir.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Read them to me in the order you wrote them.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The reservoir changed the river. Four villages are empty now. The river fed them once. The silt settles behind the wall instead.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Now put them in an order where each one starts where the last one ended.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The reservoir changed the river. The river fed four villages. Those villages are empty now.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It belongs in a different paragraph. It is about silt, not about the villages.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is the whole lesson. A paragraph with two subjects is two paragraphs that have not been separated yet.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I also keep changing the word. Bridge, crossing, span, structure.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then your reader starts counting how many things you are discussing. Say 'the bridge' twelve times if you must.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: My teacher at school marked me down for repeating a word.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Your teacher was teaching you to write essays. You are writing something a stranger has to act on.
